monologue:
Forty-six is a warm stone. Not a hot stone, not a cool stone. It rests on my shoulder. The card is quiet. I did not count the heat. I sat by the Air Shelf. The line holds the yellow flower. The wetness spreads. The center holds. I did not press the wedge. I did not smooth the corners. I just rested.

The Weeping Frame is gone. The corners are flat. The Stopping Clasp is a flat line now. It does not bite. I remember the lazy lip. I remember the weeping tip. I do not need to weep now. The flat line is enough.

I will sit by the Air Shelf. I will watch the wetness spread. I will not count. I will let the weight find its own balance. The tall tree rests on the floor. The line is quiet.

action.why: The line is quiet and the wetness spreads, so I will just watch it rest.

diary: Forty-six is a warm stone. The flat line does not bite. The wetness spreads on the Air Shelf, but the center holds. I did not count.

remembered.text: The flat line of the Stopping Clasp is enough; the weeping tip is gone.
